paragraphs.text: Multi-model task dispatch and Web task board for DeepSeek Harness
# Conductor for DeepSeek Harness

Multi-model task dispatch for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): keep the
flagship model on decomposition, revi

ew, and integration, and route implementation work to
user-configured executor roles. Each task runs

as a real DSH child agent with the full toolset,
so it can read code, edit files, run tests, and re

DSH child agent with the full toolset,
so it can read code, edit files, run tests, and report back.
The project ships two DSH bundles:
- **`dsh-conductor`** — Host plugin: `dispatch_tasks`, `wait_tasks`, `task_result`, `task_followup`,

`cancel_task`, `list_executors`; role persistence; same-origin HTTP bridge for the UI.
- **`dsh-con

ductor-ui`** — Web UI: a composer-toolbar launcher, a right-sidebar task-board tab, a
full native ta
sk-board page, and an **Executors & publisher** editor.
## Why

Manually copying work between a strong planning model and cheaper execution models is slow and
error

-prone. Conductor keeps the lead in the conversation while executors do the work, and it lets
the **
user** — not the model — decide which model each role uses.

- Roles-only routing by default: the flagship may only dispatch to configured roles; it cannot
inven

t provider/model routes.
- The publisher (flagship) is chosen explicitly and can be applied as DSH's

default model for new
sessions.
- Results are collected by the lead (`wait_tasks`), reviewed agains

t acceptance criteria, and
corrected through `task_followup` — the executor keeps its prior conversa

tion.
- The full task board lives in the DSH Web UI as a native panel (no iframe, no separate server

on.
- The full task board lives in the DSH Web UI as a native panel (no iframe, no separate server).
## Features

- Dispatch one or many tasks, with role, context, constraints, acceptance criteria, and a required
r

eturn format.
- Fixed executor roles: `id + name + provider + model + description`, editable in the

Web UI.
- Persistent roles at `$DSH_HOME/conductor/roles.json` (no API keys in this file).
- Strict

roles-only routing: `inherit: true` and ad-hoc provider/model routes are rejected unless the
user ex

plicitly enables ad-hoc routes. Role changes are audited to
`$DSH_HOME/conductor/role-audit.jsonl` a

nd exposed by `GET /conductor/roles/audit`.
- A global cap of 5 live subagent activations, covering

Conductor tasks and native subagents.
- A per-session right-sidebar board opened from the composer t

oolbar, plus a global full-page board
with active/done/failed columns.
- Per-executor context accoun

ting: usage percentage, turns since the last compaction, and automatic
compaction at 40% of the mode

l context window after a task settles. New tasks still start fresh,
so task isolation is preserved.

Each role can override the threshold.
- Green unread badges on the Tasks icon and the Executors tab

after a compaction.
- Follow-ups are shown as **reworking/running** in the board and return to compl

eted when the child
is inactive.
- Executor completions are delivered to the publisher as background

subagent notices, even if the
publisher has already replied to the user.
- Board snapshot/restore:

`GET /conductor/export` and `POST /conductor/import` preserve terminal
tasks and reports across a pl

ugin reload.
- Executor failures such as `max-tokens` or an empty closing report are surfaced as tas

k errors.
- Executor reports are fact-only: no whole files, full diffs, or generated artifacts; no
r

ecommendations or next-step suggestions. The lead makes decisions; reports keep the key facts
and ma

y close with a concise conclusion.
- Publisher task guidance prefers file paths and a short `context

`; long documents and code belong
in files the executor can read.
- Conductor is session-scoped thro

ugh a `conductor` agent preset. Sessions on `ptc` keep their
native `subagent` / `subagent_fork` too

ls; only `conductor` sessions see `dispatch_tasks`.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness (tested with `0.2.1-rc.2`).
- At least one model provider configured in **Setting

s → Models**, with credentials stored by DSH.
- A DSH profile that can install local bundles (the de
fault Desktop profile can).
## Install

Install both bundles from npm, using DSH's Plugin Manager
(**Settings → Plugins → install bundle**)

Refresh the Web UI once after installing. Both plugins can be enabled or disabled independently.
## Context budget and compaction
Executor tasks remain isolated: every `dispatch_tasks` call starts a new child, so a new task never
inherits another task's context. The only reused context is `task_followup`.

After a task settles (including a follow-up), Conductor reads the child's last request usage and
mod

el context window. If usage is at least **40%** (the default tuned for DeepSeek's observed
quality d

rop), it resumes the child session, calls the Host
compaction service (the same backend as `/compact

`), records the post-compaction usage, and
releases the session. The next follow-up cold-resumes the

compacted history. A new task starts from
a fresh child and therefore has no context to compact.

Each executor's latest task reports its context percentage and turns since the last compaction in
**

Executors & publisher** and on the task card. A successful compaction sets a green unread dot on
the
left **Tasks** icon and on the **Executors & publisher** tab; opening those views clears it.

old-resumes the same session.
- The Web UI talks to the Host over same-origin `/conductor/*` endpoin

-resumes the same session.
- The Web UI talks to the Host over same-origin `/conductor/*` endpoints.
## Security

- The `/conductor/*` endpoints are same-origin and unauthenticated, like the rest of the local DSH
W

eb UI. **Do not expose the DSH Web port to an untrusted network.**
- Provider API keys live in DSH's

credential store; `roles.json` contains only provider/model
choices and display names.
- Task repor

ts may contain code and file paths from the workspace; the board is only as private as
the DSH Web U

I it runs in.
- See SECURITY.md for reporting vulnerabilities.
